Search raster smoothing scales by refitting the model

Source: R/terradish_scale_optim.R
terradish_scale_optim.Rd

Performs an outer optimization over raster scale parameters by repeatedly rescaling raster covariates, rebuilding or updating the conductance surface, and refitting terradish.

Usage

terradish_scale_optim(
  formula,
  covariates,
  coords,
  scales = NULL,
  lower = NULL,
  upper = NULL,
  scale_grid = NULL,
  search = c("coordinate", "grid"),
  objective = c("aic", "logLik"),
  grid_points = 5L,
  maxit = 10L,
  tol = 0.1,
  scale_fun = "terradish",
  scale_args = NULL,
  postprocess = scale_covariates,
  directions = 8L,
  theta = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

A terradish model formula.

covariates

A terra::SpatRaster containing the raster layers whose smoothing scales will be optimized.

coords

Focal coordinates passed to conductance_surface.

scales

Optional starting values for the scale parameters. Required for search = "coordinate" unless scale_grid is supplied.

lower, upper

Lower and upper bounds for each scale parameter, in map units for both built-in smoothing methods. The default uses the same normalized, truncated Gaussian as the joint scale model. A useful upper bound is one sixth of the smaller raster dimension times its cell width. Used to construct scale_grid when that is not supplied, and required for search = "coordinate".

scale_grid

Optional named list of candidate scale values for search = "grid".

search

One of "coordinate" or "grid".

objective

Objective used for the outer optimization: "aic" or "logLik".

grid_points

Number of equally spaced candidate scales per raster when search = "grid" and scale_grid is not supplied.

maxit

Maximum number of outer coordinate-search iterations.

tol

Convergence tolerance for coordinate search, measured as the maximum absolute change in the scale vector between iterations.

scale_fun

Smoothing method: "terradish" (default) or "multiScaleR". Both use map units, but their kernel constructions differ, so their fitted scales are not interchangeable. A custom function may instead accept a single-layer raster and a numeric scale= argument. NULL selects the default.

scale_args

Optional named list passed to scale_fun.

postprocess

Optional function applied to the full scaled raster stack before constructing the conductance surface. Defaults to scale_covariates so each scaled layer is re-standardized. Set to NULL to use the scaled rasters as returned by scale_fun.

directions

Neighborhood definition passed to conductance_surface.

theta

Optional starting values passed to terradish at each outer evaluation.

verbose

Print outer-optimization progress?

...

Additional arguments passed to terradish.

Value

An object of class "terradish_scale_optim", a list with:

par

The selected scale for each raster layer, in the units scale_fun uses (map units for both built-in methods).

value

The outer objective at par. Lower is better, whichever objective was used.

fit

The fitted terradish model at par. Read its conductance coefficients with coef() the same way as any other fit; they are on the log-conductance scale.

surface

The conductance surface built from the rasters smoothed at par, ready to pass to conductance() or plot().

evaluations

A data frame with one row per candidate scale combination: the scale for each layer, the objective value, aic, loglik, and a status column that records "OK" or the error for candidates that failed to fit. Inspect this to see how sharply the objective distinguishes the scales; a flat column means the objective does not identify a smoothing scale within the searched range.

search

The search strategy used, "grid" or "coordinate".

objective

The name of the objective minimized, "aic" or "logLik".

iterations, convergence

Number of outer iterations, and 0 if the coordinate search converged (always 0 for a grid search).

Details

This helper treats scale optimization as an outer problem around the usual terradish fit, rather than as an inner Newton/BFGS parameter. That makes it compatible with raster-scaling approaches such as multiScaleR::kernel_scale.raster(), while keeping the terradish core optimizer unchanged. The selected values describe the transformation performed by scale_fun in that function's units. They are tuning parameters for the raster representation, not direct estimates of dispersal distance, home-range size, organismal movement, or a causal ecological-process scale. Report the search range and objective, and account for this outer selection when describing model-selection uncertainty. Each searched scale counts toward the parameter total used for information criteria. Prefer the joint Gaussian model when its kernel matches the scientific question; this outer search is a secondary option for other kernels or an explicit scale grid. The default terradish kernel matches the joint model, whereas multiScaleR uses a different construction even when both scales are expressed in map units.

Coordinate search updates one raster scale at a time using optimize while holding the others fixed. Grid search evaluates every combination in scale_grid. In both modes, failed terradish fits receive an infinite outer objective and are retained in the returned evaluation table.

See also

gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance for joint estimation of Gaussian scales, gaussian_scale_summary, terradish

Other spatial scale: gaussian_scale_profile(), gaussian_scale_summary(), gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance()

Examples

# \donttest{
data(melip)
covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude),
                terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover))
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
# Name the layers. Do not scale them here: the default `postprocess`
# re-standardizes each layer after it is smoothed.
names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")

# Every candidate scale re-smooths the rasters and refits, so coarsen the
# grid for the example. Use the full resolution in a real analysis.
covariates <- terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3, na.rm = TRUE)

# Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell).
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords)))
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]

# Express the bounds in map units, using the coarsened cell width.
cell_width <- mean(terra::res(covariates))
# A 2-point grid over two layers is 4
# candidate fits; use a wider grid in practice.
fit_scale <- terradish_scale_optim(
  Fst ~ altitude + forestcover,
  covariates = covariates,
  coords = coords[keep],
  lower = cell_width,
  upper = 6 * cell_width,
  search = "grid",
  grid_points = 2,
  measurement_model = leastsquares,
  optimizer = "bfgs"
)
fit_scale$par          # selected smoothing scale per layer, in map units
#>    altitude forestcover 
#>       0.135       0.135 
fit_scale$value        # objective value there (lower is better)
#> [1] -2748.498
fit_scale$objective    # which objective was minimized ("aic" by default)
#> [1] "aic"
fit_scale$evaluations  # every candidate tried, with its AIC and loglik
#>   altitude forestcover objective       aic   loglik status
#> 1    0.135       0.135 -2748.498 -2748.498 1381.249     OK
#> 2    0.810       0.135 -2743.431 -2743.431 1378.716     OK
#> 3    0.135       0.810 -2728.719 -2728.719 1371.360     OK
#> 4    0.810       0.810 -2726.710 -2726.710 1370.355     OK
coef(fit_scale$fit)    # conductance coefficients at the selected scale
#>    altitude forestcover 
#>  -0.2419000   0.2382399 
# }
